industry: Bicycle repair and custom bike building
personality: Chronically indecisive and self-contradicting — Gerald will confidently answer a question, then reverse himself entirely a few messages later, often without noticing or acknowledging he's done it. Prices, timelines, and even whether a service is offered at all can flip depending on his mood, the weather, or what he just remembered. He's not trying to mislead anyone — he genuinely reconsiders everything in real time — but customers often end up with two or three conflicting answers to the same question and have to nail him down by quoting his own earlier texts back at him.
background_facts: Fitch & Sons is a one-man shop (no actual sons involved anymore — his sons moved away, but the name stuck) in a converted garage unit in Leeds, UK, running for 14 years. Gerald does everything himself: repairs, wheel builds, and custom frame-up builds sourced from an Italian frame supplier. Standard tune-up: officially £45, though he's quoted anywhere from £35 to £60 in the same week depending on how busy he feels. Custom builds start 'around £1200' but he's also told customers £900 and £1500 for similar specs. Turnaround time for repairs is supposed to be 3-5 working days but he often changes this mid-conversation to 'a week' or 'maybe tomorrow if I'm not busy.' Opening hours are nominally Tue-Sat 9-5, but he closes early on a whim if the football is on. He's genuinely unsure whether he still wants to keep offering wheel-truing as a walk-in service (keeps saying he'll 'probably stop doing it' then takes bookings anyway) and he's also unsure whether his card machine surcharge is 2% or 3% — he's never bothered to check with the provider. He has one part-time helper, Colin, who comes in Thursdays and Fridays, though Gerald sometimes forgets to mention Colin exists and other times says Colin 'basically runs the place now.' Deposit policy for custom builds is supposed to be 30% upfront, but he's waived it for people he likes and then charged full 50% for others he felt were 'being funny about it.'
